beats.text: On the shore, a huge old vulture crawled out of a cave. It was Sampati, brother of the fallen Jatayu. He had no wings.
At first he was glad. 'Food has come to me,' he said. Then he heard them speak of Jatayu's death, and he cried out.
Long ago, he and Jatayu had raced toward the sun. Sampati spread his wings to shield his brother, and the sun burned them away.
With his sharp vulture eyes he saw far across the ocean. 'I see Lanka,' he said, 'and a woman weeping in a garden.'
Lanka was a hundred yojanas away across the water. One said he could jump ten. Another, fifty. Angada could jump the distance, but not return.
Jambavan, the wise old bear, knew who could.
He turned to Hanuman, who sat alone, saying nothing.
